blocks.text: Severe acute malnutrition is usually caused by inadequate dietary intake, disease, or a combination of both.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: A severely malnourished child may have serious infection without fever or typical inflammatory signs. Always actively assess for infection.

content_groups.group_title: C. Classification according to clinical presentation

blocks.text: Nutritional oedema, often with skin and hair changes.
Marasmic kwashiorkor: Severe wasting occurring alongside nutritional oedema.

Remember: The older classification based on percentage of expected weight-for-age (such as the Gomez classification) may appear in examinations, but WHO Z-scores, MUAC and oedema are central to current SAM assessment.

items.text: O – Oedema, usually bilateral and pitting.

blocks.text: Important: Kwashiorkor is not simply caused by isolated protein deficiency. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial and involves dietary, infectious, metabolic and environmental factors.

blocks.text: Nigeria-specific examination pearl: Consider malaria, sickle cell disease, hookworm and iron deficiency prominently in the differential diagnosis of childhood anaemia.
Management of SAM is commonly organised into three phases:

items.text: Begin cautious feeding using F-75 where indicated.
Gradually increase energy and protein intake.
Transition from F-75 to F-100 or ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF), depending on the treatment setting and clinical status.

content_groups.group_title: Ten steps of inpatient SAM management

rows: Provide sensory stimulation and emotional support
Prepare for follow-up and relapse prevention
Nutrient-dense therapeutic food, particularly in outpatient treatment of uncomplicated SAM

items.text: Avoid routine aggressive intravenous fluid administration in SAM.
Rehydration must be cautious and guided by clinical assessment and the relevant protocol.
Do not delay antibiotics in a severely malnourished child with suspected infection.
Monitor potassium, magnesium, phosphate and glucose.
Iron supplementation is generally delayed until the child is stabilised and gaining weight, according to the applicable protocol.

blocks.text: Outpatient versus inpatient management: Children with uncomplicated SAM who are clinically well, alert, have appetite and no serious medical complications may be managed through outpatient therapeutic programmes. Complicated SAM requires inpatient assessment and treatment.

Decreases maternal risk of breast and ovarian cancer

items.text: Provides colostrum, rich in immunological factors.
Reduces risk of necrotising enterocolitis in preterm infants.
Reduces lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer.
Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months.
Continue breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Colostrum should not be discarded. It is particularly valuable because of its immune-protective properties.

rows: Introduce complementary foods at around 6 months
Increase meal frequency as the child grows
Use safe, affordable, locally available foods
Include adequate energy and nutrient content
Include fruits, vegetables, animal-source foods and fortified foods
Wash hands, use safe water and clean utensils
Offer foods from different food groups
Progress from mashed to lumpy and family foods
Small amounts of soft, mashed or semi-solid foods, 2–3 meals daily
Finely chopped or mashed foods, 3–4 meals daily
Family foods in suitable textures, 3–4 meals daily with 1–2 nutritious snacks

blocks.text: These are general feeding principles; portion sizes and frequency should be adjusted to the child's appetite, growth and nutritional needs.

items.text: G – Grains and cereals: rice, maize, millet, oats.
A – Animal-source foods: eggs, fish, meat, milk.
O – Oils and legumes: beans, groundnuts, vegetable oils.
Honey before 12 months because of infant botulism risk.
Choking hazards such as whole nuts, whole grapes and hard raw vegetables.
Tea and coffee, which can interfere with iron absorption.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Complementary feeding should be timely, adequate, safe and responsive. It should not replace breastfeeding abruptly.
